sections.html:
Barrow County is a compact 163 square miles at the eastern fringe of metro Atlanta, with Winder as its seat. Growth has been fast. The population was 21,354 in 1980, 46,144 in 2000, 69,367 in 2010 and 83,505 in 2020, and the mid-2025 estimate is 99,773.

  • Cities: Auburn, Statham and Winder
  • Towns: Bethlehem, Braselton (mostly Jackson County, partly Gwinnett and Hall) and Carl
  • Census-designated place: Russell
  • Unincorporated: Barrow Heights, Mulberry and Whistleville

Braselton spans several counties, so an owner there should check the parcel record to learn which county mails the bill.

Building has not slowed, with 1,584 permits issued in 2025. A seller in a newer subdivision near Winder or Auburn will be listed beside many similar houses, so price and condition carry extra weight.

About 78.5% of housing units are owner-occupied, and the county averages 518.5 people per square mile. In 2020, 30,019 housing units were counted and the homeowner vacancy rate was 1.5%, which points to a tight supply of houses for sale.

sections.h2: Who sends the bill and who sets the value
sections.html:
The tax commissioner works from 30 N. Broad Street, Winder, GA 30680. The phone number is (770) 307-3106, and the office answers weekdays from 8:00 to 4:30. You can also go through the Barrow County Tax Portal. Card payments carry a 2.5% service fee, minimum $1.50. For vehicle transactions, bring a Georgia driver's license or ID card showing a Barrow County address.

Values come from the Tax Assessors Office, found at that same street address, which takes calls from 8 to 5 on weekdays. The commissioner chooses the due date and mails the bill yet has no influence on your value. Your notice can be printed from qPublic.

Property notices, for real estate and for personal property such as aircraft, boats and business equipment, normally go out May 1. Final tax bills wait until September and come due in November. Your own bill sets the date that counts.

Do not pay from a notice. It only estimates the tax on your assessed value. To dispute it, file within 45 days using qPublic, the mail, or a visit to the Tax Assessors Office.

  • Grounds you can use: taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption
  • Tracks: Board of Equalization, hearing officer or arbitrator
  • On a single parcel, state revenue officials have no power to overturn a board, hearing officer, arbitrator or court

Weekday calls to the assessors are welcome for questions on a notice or the appeal steps. Anyone planning a challenge should phone early, well inside the 45 days.

sections.h2: What you can look up online
sections.html:
Two sites cover most of it. The tax portal lets you search any property in the county, pay property tax and renew car tags. The assessors' qPublic pages let you print current and prior year notices from the assessment section, which helps when a buyer's agent asks what the value was last year.

Mind the returned-check rule on the tax portal. If your bank dishonors a check, a service fee is added under state law, and the county uses Envision Payment Solutions for recovery, reachable at 1-877-290-5460. For a closing, a certified payment avoids the problem, and the portal's property search is a quick way to confirm the parcel details before you sign.

A house inside a city limit may owe the city as well as the county, so the city clerk can tell you whether a second bill exists. With three cities and three towns in the county, a county payoff may not cover what a municipality is owed.

Under Georgia law, whoever owns the house on January 1 owes the entire year, even with a sale on January 2, and part-year refunds are not given. Have the title company get a fresh payoff from each billing office and pay both at closing. Splitting the cost with the buyer is something your closing paperwork handles.

Behind on an earlier year? The commissioner's office can say whether a lien was recorded. Ask before accepting an offer, since any recorded lien must be cleared before closing.

sections.h2: Before you list: a short checklist
sections.html:
Have your paperwork ready before the first showing and a Barrow County sale runs more smoothly. Take these steps in order.

  1. Print this year's and last year's assessment notices from qPublic for the buyer's agent.
  2. Phone (770) 307-3106 for the amount owed on the parcel, earlier unpaid years included.
  3. Ask about recorded liens, and check with the city clerk for a municipal bill if you are in Auburn, Statham, Winder or another town.
  4. Put in the contract who pays this year's bill. The county will not split it.
  5. Pass the payoff figures from every billing office to the title company.

If you dispute the value, the 45 days count from the notice date and not from the day you decide to sell. Look at the notice date the moment it arrives, because a late filing will not be heard.

Selling for cash as-is tends to close quicker, with no lender appraisal and no haggling over repairs. The tax steps above still apply, and the balance comes out of your proceeds at the table.

sections.h2: Surplus money after a tax sale
sections.html:
The county handles tax sale surplus through Weissman Excess Funds Management. The firm publishes open records on the funds it handles, typically refreshed on the 1st and 15th of each month, and you request information by email.

Barrow County does not release excess funds to third parties. Someone who lost property to a tax sale should contact the Tax Commissioner's Office or the firm directly about a claim, rather than pay a stranger to chase it.

Owners who make a house their primary residence qualify for a standard Georgia homestead exemption, and many counties add larger local ones. Depending on the county, you file with the tax commissioner or the assessors.

Phone (770) 307-3106 to find out which Barrow County office takes yours, and bring proof of residency. The exemption comes off assessed value first, and then the millage rate hits what is left.

If you are the one selling, an exemption you hold does not pass to the buyer. The new owner has to apply in their own name, so mention it to their agent and save them a surprise on the first bill.

faqs.q: Where is the Barrow County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: Its office is at 30 N. Broad Street, Winder, GA 30680. Phone (770) 307-3106 any weekday from 8:00 to 4:30.

faqs.q: Does a Barrow County assessment notice require payment?
faqs.a: No. A notice only estimates the tax from your assessed value. The real bills usually follow in September.

faqs.q: What is the way to appeal a Barrow County value?
faqs.a: File within 45 days of the notice, online through qPublic, by mail, or at the Tax Assessors Office, 30 N. Broad Street.

faqs.q: Are tax sale surplus funds paid out to third parties in Barrow County?
faqs.a: No. The county does not release excess funds to third parties, and claims run through the Tax Commissioner's Office and its excess funds partner.

faqs.q: Who pays if I sell a Barrow County house mid-year?
faqs.a: Georgia law makes the January 1 owner liable for the full year, with no part-year refund. Split the bill with the buyer in the closing paperwork.
